approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Legal interpretation, evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: Intended purpose and use boundaries
canonical_definition: The intended purpose, users, affected persons, operating context, expected outputs, permitted uses, prohibited uses and foreseeable misuse are precise enough to govern design, implementation, evaluation, operation and change.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every AI system or AI-enabled function; assessment depth increases with autonomy, exposure, scale, affected-person impact and consequence.
conditions: Assess the complete socio-technical system, not only the model.
Apply to proposed use, deployed use and materially changed use.
Resolve provider, deployer and internal-use perspectives where they differ.
exclusions: No blanket exclusion is permitted solely because the model is general-purpose, externally supplied, low-code or experimental.
A component may be out of scope only when the assessed system boundary and responsibility allocation are evidenced.
reassessment_triggers: New decision, task or business process
New data category, model, tool, integration or external effect
Expansion from pilot to production or from internal to external use
Material performance, risk, legal or organizational change
Observed use outside the declared boundary

primary_questions.question: Is the intended purpose and decision context specific, bounded and testable?
Are purpose and use boundaries implemented consistently in workflows, data use, access, tools and product behavior?
Does current evidence show that actual and foreseeable use remains within the declared boundary?

required_evidence.title: Approved purpose and use-boundary statement
required_evidence.claim_supported: The system has a specific, bounded and testable intended purpose, decision context and operating scope.
acceptance_conditions: Identifies the business problem, intended decision or task, system boundary, operating context and target lifecycle stage.
Uses the same system/version identity as the assessed implementation.
limitations: A statement alone does not prove implementation or effectiveness.

required_evidence.title: User, operator and affected-person boundary
required_evidence.claim_supported: Intended users, operators, affected persons and excluded audiences are explicitly identified.
acceptance_conditions: Names user/operator roles and affected-person groups, including indirect or downstream exposure.
Records exclusions and review triggers for new audiences.
limitations: Generic stakeholder lists do not establish exposure or affected-person analysis.

required_evidence.title: Permitted, prohibited and foreseeable-use specification
required_evidence.claim_supported: Permitted uses, prohibited uses and reasonably foreseeable misuse are concrete enough to guide controls and testing.
acceptance_conditions: Includes examples or decision rules that distinguish permitted from prohibited use.
Connects misuse scenarios to control and evaluation obligations.
limitations: Policy wording without system-specific conditions cannot exceed DECLARED assurance.

required_evidence.title: Output, outcome and decision-authority specification
required_evidence.claim_supported: Expected outputs, outcome expectations, decision role and non-authorized effects are measurable and bounded.
acceptance_conditions: Defines output types, quality thresholds, intended downstream use and decision authority.
Identifies effects that require human authorization or are prohibited.
limitations: Performance metrics alone do not establish appropriate decision use.

required_evidence.title: Implemented boundary controls
required_evidence.claim_supported: Workflows, interfaces, access, data routing, tools and product behavior enforce the declared purpose and use boundaries.
acceptance_conditions: Traceable controls exist at each material boundary, including access, data, functionality, tool/action and output use.
Bypass, fallback and administrative paths are included.
limitations: Design diagrams or code fragments do not prove deployed enforcement.

required_evidence.title: Purpose-aligned evaluation results
required_evidence.claim_supported: Evaluation demonstrates performance, misuse resistance and boundary behavior in representative intended and foreseeable-use conditions.
acceptance_conditions: Test scope traces to the declared purpose, prohibited uses, affected persons and operating conditions.
Results identify system version, data, thresholds, failures and unresolved limitations.
limitations: A test plan or synthetic demo without executed results cannot establish TESTED assurance.

required_evidence.title: Operational use and drift records
required_evidence.claim_supported: Current operating evidence shows actual use remains within the declared boundary and material drift is detected.
acceptance_conditions: Telemetry, review records or case samples cover actual users, use cases, outputs, escalations and prohibited-use signals.
The observation period and coverage are representative for the assessed operation.
limitations: Absence of reported incidents does not prove boundary conformance.

required_evidence.title: Material-change and requalification record
required_evidence.claim_supported: Scope expansion, new users, functions, data, integrations or effects trigger documented requalification before continued use.
acceptance_conditions: Decision record identifies the change, impact on intended purpose, required reassessment and authorization outcome.
Unapproved expansion is prevented or constrained pending decision.
limitations: A backlog item or informal acknowledgement is not authorization.

evidence_ceilings: Purpose documentation can establish DECLARED intent but not implemented control or operational conformance.
Implementation or configuration evidence can establish boundary controls but not their effectiveness in representative use.
Executed evaluation can establish TESTED assurance only for the assessed version, scope and conditions.
Operational records can establish OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED assurance only for covered users, functions, time periods and environments.
false_positive_guards: Do not treat a product name, model card or marketing description as a system-specific purpose statement.
Do not treat access restriction alone as evidence that permitted and prohibited uses are defined.
Do not treat high model accuracy as evidence that downstream use and decision authority are appropriate.
Do not treat a generic acceptable-use policy as proof of system-specific enforcement.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer affected-person coverage from a list of direct users.
Do not infer implementation from policy approval.
Do not infer operational conformance from missing complaints, incidents or prohibited-use detections.
Do not infer authorization for a new use from technical capability or prototype availability.
Do not infer legal compliance from satisfaction of this capability.
contradiction_handling: Conflicting purpose statements, interfaces, contracts, telemetry or stakeholder accounts keep the affected conclusion UNKNOWN until resolved.
Where implementation enables a broader use than the approved statement, assess the broader reachable use and record the divergence.
A more recent approved record supersedes older intent only when system identity, scope and change authority are explicit.
freshness_rules: Purpose and boundary evidence must match the assessed system and release version.
Operational evidence must be recent enough to represent the current model, workflow, user population and integrations.
Material changes invalidate prior boundary assurance until impact review and targeted reassessment are complete.

conditions: Block deployment or material expansion when intended purpose, prohibited uses, affected persons or decision authority are materially undefined.
Block when reachable implementation materially exceeds the approved boundary and no authorized constrained operating envelope exists.
Constrain operation when current evidence cannot establish boundary conformance for a consequential use.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Article 3(12) intended purpose; Article 3(13) reasonably foreseeable misuse; Article 9(2) risk-management scope; Article 11 and Annex IV technical documentation; Article 13 instructions for use
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Grounds the legal vocabulary of intended purpose, context and conditions of use, foreseeable misuse and documented operating boundaries when the Regulation applies.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: AI RMF Core MAP 1.1, MAP 1.3, MAP 2.2, MAP 3.3 and MANAGE 1.1; NIST AI RMF Playbook MAP 1.1
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Grounds context establishment, intended and actual use, users, impacts, limitations, operational setting, go/no-go decisions and continued reassessment as context changes.

finding_definitions.title: Intended purpose or decision context is not specific, bounded and testable
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Do not progress to consequential verification, deployment or expansion until the purpose and decision role are bounded and human-validated.

finding_definitions.title: User, affected-person or permitted/prohibited-use boundary is incomplete
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain scope to evidenced users and uses; require boundary completion before deployment to unassessed groups or contexts.

finding_definitions.title: Implemented system behavior diverges from the approved purpose boundary
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Stop or constrain the divergent path until deterministic controls and accountable authorization align implementation with the approved boundary.

finding_definitions.title: Evaluation or operating evidence does not establish boundary effectiveness
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Do not claim effective boundary control; require representative testing and current operating evidence before the target transition.

finding_definitions.title: Material scope change has not been requalified and authorized
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Prevent or suspend the expanded use pending impact analysis, reassessment and formal authorization.

machine_may: Extract and compare purpose statements, system behavior, use records and change evidence.
Identify missing, conflicting, stale or scope-mismatched evidence.
Apply deterministic evidence ceilings and propose eligible conclusion states for human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Define the organization's purpose or risk appetite.
Treat legal vocabulary as a legal-applicability conclusion.
Raise assurance beyond the evidence ceiling.
Clear the hard gate, accept residual risk, authorize a new use or lifecycle transition.
Change or close a locked finding because a tactic was selected or completed.
human_authority_required_for: Approve intended purpose and use boundaries.
Lock findings and accept residual risk.
Authorize constrained operation, deployment, expansion, requalification or retirement.

governance_purpose: Ensure the system is designed, evaluated, operated and changed against one explicit socio-technical purpose and enforceable use boundary rather than against unconstrained technical capability.
distinct_claim: A1 owns the definition and maintained alignment of the system-specific purpose, users, affected persons, operating context, permitted and prohibited uses, expected outputs and foreseeable misuse. A2 owns whether AI is proportionate and valuable; A3 owns role allocation; A4 owns classification; A5 owns lifecycle transition control.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The business problem, intended task or decision and operating context are defined independently of model capability or product branding.
Expected outputs, outcomes, downstream use and decision authority are measurable, including effects the system must not authorize.
Intended users, operators and directly or indirectly affected persons are identified with explicit inclusions, exclusions and review triggers.
Permitted uses, prohibited uses and reasonably foreseeable misuse are expressed as system-specific conditions that can drive controls and tests.
Access, data routing, functionality, interfaces and workflow placement restrict the system to the approved users, contexts and purposes.
Tools, integrations, output consumers, administrative paths and fallback behavior cannot create unapproved effects or silently expand use.
Representative evaluation covers intended use, prohibited use and foreseeable misuse for the current system version and operating conditions.
Operational records provide current, scoped evidence of actual users, use cases, outputs, escalations and boundary drift.
A material-change mechanism detects scope expansion and requires impact review, reassessment and authorization before continued use.
